chunks: Ahmad b. Harun al-Fami (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Ja'far b. Batta narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Ishaq b. Sa'd narrated to us from Bakr b. Muhammad from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said:

People on Friday are of three states: A man who attends it attentively and silently before the Imam -- that is an expiation for his sins from one Friday to the next, plus three extra days, because of the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
'Whoever comes with a good deed shall have tenfold the like of it.' [6:160]

And a man who attends it in commotion, flattery, and restlessness -- so that is his lot. And a man who attends it while the Imam delivers the sermon, then stands up to pray -- he has erred in the Sunna, and he is of those who, when he asks Allah Mighty and Majestic, if He wills He grants him, and if He wills He deprives him.

key_terms.إنصات: Attentive silence (insat) - listening carefully without speaking
key_terms.الجمعة: Friday prayer (al-Jumu'a) - the congregational prayer on Friday
key_terms.السنة: The Prophetic practice (al-Sunna) - the established way of the Prophet

ai.seo_question: What are the three states of people at Friday prayer according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) categorizes Friday prayer attendees into three groups. The first attends quietly and attentively, earning forgiveness for ten days' worth of sins, citing Quran 6:160 as proof that a good deed is multiplied tenfold. The second attends but is distracted and disruptive, gaining nothing. The third prays during the sermon, violating the prophetic practice, and is left to Allah's discretion regarding his supplications.

en.bilal-muhammad: Ahmad b. Harun al-Fami (ra) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Ja`far b. Batta narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Ishaq b. Sa`id narrated to us from Bakr b. Muhammad from al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (as). He said: Amir al-Mu'minin (as) said:

People on Friday are of three states: (1) a man who witnesses it attentively and silently before the Imam – that will be a forgiveness of his sins from Friday until the next Friday, plus three days, because of the saying of Allah,
“Whoever comes with a good deed will have ten like it.” [6:160]

(2) A man who witnesses it in commotion, noise, and annoyance – so that will be his omen. (3) A man who witnesses it, and the Imam delivers the sermon, so he rises to pray, but he makes a mistake in the sunna – so that will be up to the will of Allah, whether He grants it or forbids it.
